svg.title: Score matching on and off the model class
svg.desc: Left: a two-well quartic density and its score-matching fit at r = 4, which coincides with it exactly, and the r = 2 Gaussian fit for contrast. Middle: a two-Gaussian mixture, which is outside the family; the r = 4 score-matching fit is visibly worse than the MaxEnt fit (L1 errors 0.29 and 0.22). Right: the fitted energies at r = 6 and r = 8 over five standard deviations. The r = 6 energy falls to minus infinity in both tails, so it is not a density; the r = 8 energy has a deep well near minus 3.8 standard deviations, far from the data, where all of its probability mass ends up.
svg.text: Score matching fits the score where the data is, and nowhere else
The Fisher divergence weighs score errors by p(x): where p ≈ 0 the polynomial is free. MaxEnt stays normalisable at every r (L1 0.62 → 0.10).
